title: Entrust each kept thing to a named custodian
wire: A keepsake without a custodian is a wish; name the person or role that carries it.

title: Make the handoff inspectable by its receiver
wire: A successor should recover purpose, location, and next action without private context.

title: Name what is allowed to lapse
wire: Declare which items may be released so retention attention is not spread falsely thin.

title: Record what was deliberately not kept
wire: A documented release narrows the successor's search space and honours the choice.

title: Refuse the infallible-archive claim
wire: Preservation describes intent and custody, never a guarantee of persistence.

title: Record where each kept thing came from
wire: State provenance so a successor can judge what the kept thing is and is not.

title: Name what is being kept before how
wire: State the thing preserved, its boundary, and why it outlives the keeper.

title: Give living keepsakes a review cadence
wire: Relationships and practices decay silently; set when each is next reviewed.

title: Invite review before the entrustment is relied on
wire: A second reader can expose a custodian or a route the keeper stopped seeing.

title: Rehearse the succession at least once
wire: A handoff that has never been practised is a plan, not a proven route.

title: Keep changes to a kept thing reviewable
wire: Record each increment so its history can be read, reverted, and entrusted intact.
